title: Network Replay and Consistency Across Testbeds
problem: Shared network testbeds introduce variability (jitter, loss) that degrades experiment fidelity and reproducibility; difficult to quantify testbed quality.
motivation: Precise network behavior reproduction is essential for reliable systems research; current testbeds lack tools to measure and compare consistency.
method: Choir: 100 Gbps network replay tool running on commodity hardware with novel consistency metric for cross-testbed comparison.
key_novelty: First 100 Gbps replay tool for shared infrastructures; quantitative consistency metric enables testbed quality assessment.
contributions: 100 Gbps network replay engine for commodity hardware
Novel consistency metric for testbed comparison
Empirical demonstration that shared testbeds (e.g., FABRIC) have significantly higher variability than local bare-metal systems

metrics.latency_variability: Order of magnitude increase under high utilization

limitations: Limited to network replay; doesn't propose solutions to reduce variability; testbed-specific evaluation.
